open_points.subject: AllocationInstruction and ExpenseAllocation precision
open_points.text: M26 calls AllocationInstruction an "unbounded Decimal" whose amounts are "otherwise unconstrained", and M29 stores the amount "as instructed"; the modeling convention and A9 instead require all stored money to have exactly 2 fraction digits.
open_points.question: May an allocation with more than two fraction digits be accepted and stored, or must it be rejected or quantized to two digits before the allocation-sum check?
options: Accept and store arbitrary Decimal precision when the exact allocation sum equals the expense total
Reject any allocation amount that is not already exact to two fraction digits
Round each allocation ROUND_HALF_UP to two digits before checking and storing the sum
open_points.default_guess: Accept arbitrary finite Decimal precision because the changed text explicitly accepts the current unbounded-Decimal service behavior.

witness.initial: An active project has an authorized operator creating a confirmed EUR expense with total_amount 10.00.
events: The operator supplies allocations of 0.001 and 9.999 whose exact sum is 10.00.
outcomes: The intake succeeds and stores both allocation amounts as instructed under M26/M29.
The intake is refused because A9 says stored amounts are already 2-digit exact; alternatively an implementation rounds them before the sum check.
witness.observer: The operator sees success versus refusal, and later staff and viewers can see different allocation values.

open_points.subject: Boundary handling of excess fractional precision for non-allocation money
open_points.text: A9 says "Decimal, 2 fraction digits, ROUND_HALF_UP at derivation boundaries; stored amounts are already 2-digit exact" but does not say what an input boundary does with a present monetary value having more than two fraction digits.
open_points.question: For non-allocation monetary inputs with excess fractional precision, must the boundary reject them, round them half-up, or accept them until storage?
options: Reject values with more than two fraction digits
Round half-up to two digits before validation and storage
Accept the value and rely on persistence or a later derivation to quantize it
open_points.default_guess: Reject excess precision because rounding is named only for derivation boundaries and stored amounts must already be exact.

witness.initial: An active project has an authorized operator and no payment with a newly supplied payment_id.
events: The operator registers a WorkPayment with amount 1.005 EUR.
outcomes: The operation rejects the amount as not already having two fraction digits.
The operation rounds it half-up and stores 1.01 EUR.
witness.observer: The operator sees refusal versus a successful payment, and project viewers see different payment totals.

open_points.subject: Rounding and aggregation of higher-precision allocation-derived totals
open_points.text: The change permits unbounded allocation Decimal values, while A9 only says to use ROUND_HALF_UP "at derivation boundaries" and does not identify whether allocation-derived totals are rounded per allocation, per target/section, or only after aggregation.
open_points.question: If higher-precision allocations are accepted, at which stage are section actuals, material actual totals, and Other expenses totals rounded, and must aggregate totals equal the sum of the displayed rounded components?
options: Sum exact stored allocations per section, round each displayed section, and sum those rounded section results for displayed totals
Sum all exact allocations for each aggregate and round each aggregate independently
Round every allocation before any per-target or aggregate sum
open_points.default_guess: Sum exact values per displayed component, round components to two digits, and derive displayed aggregate totals from those rounded components.

witness.initial: An active budget has sections A and B, and an included expense totals 10.00 EUR.
events: An operator stores allocations of 0.005 to A, 0.005 to B, and 9.990 to Other expenses.
A staff member or viewer reads the BudgetView.
outcomes: A and B each display 0.01 and material_actual_total displays 0.02 because it sums displayed section results.
A and B each display 0.01 but material_actual_total displays 0.01 because the exact section allocations are aggregated before rounding.
witness.observer: Staff and viewers see a material total that either does or does not equal the sum of the displayed section actuals.

open_points.subject: Overall progress result precision
open_points.text: A9 defines overall progress as "Σ(work_planned × percent) / Σ(work_planned)" and says ROUND_HALF_UP at derivation boundaries, but it does not specify the result scale for this non-monetary Decimal percentage.
open_points.question: To how many fractional digits is overall_progress_percent rounded, and is that quantization part of the observable result?
options: Return an integer percentage rounded half-up
Use a fixed precision other than two digits
Return the Decimal division result under the implementation's decimal context
open_points.default_guess: Round to two fractional digits using ROUND_HALF_UP.

witness.initial: The active budget has section A with work_planned 1.00 and recorded progress 1%, and section B with work_planned 2.00 and recorded progress 2%.
events: A staff member or viewer requests the progress view.
outcomes: overall_progress_percent is returned as 1.67 after two-place half-up quantization.
overall_progress_percent is returned with another precision, such as 1.6667, or is affected by the implementation's Decimal context.
witness.observer: The staff member or viewer sees a different overall progress percentage.
